topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Cache Utilization
explanation: The memory hierarchy organizes storage levels (registers, L1/L2/L3, DRAM) to minimize CPU-memory latency by balancing speed and capacity. Caches are high-speed, low-latency components that store frequently accessed subsets of data from slower, larger levels. Optimal cache utilization maximizes the *cache hit rate*, ensuring the CPU finds required data in the fastest tier. Data is transferred between levels in fixed-size blocks called *cache lines*. High program performance relies on structuring data access patterns to exploit *temporal locality* and *spatial locality*, thereby minimizing costly *cache misses* and subsequent main memory access.
